key_insight: Local splitting and merging in disordered porous media produce pore-body flow rates that follow a Gamma distribution, which then determines throat flow statistics.
engineering_relevance: The model links flow-rate variability to simple geometric descriptors like pore-throat width variation, enabling low-parameter prediction of flow in porous materials.
method: Steady Stokes flow in 2D disordered arrays of circular obstacles
Pore-network model with local flow correlations at junctions
Derive pore-body Gamma distribution and infer throat-rate distribution from geometry
evidence_signal: The predictions agree closely with CFD simulations and outperform prior mean-field models that ignore local flow-rate correlations.
watch_item: The framework is derived for steady 2D Stokes flow, so extension to 3D, inertia-dominated, or strongly transient regimes may require revalidation.
paper_title: Topological origin of flow distributions in disordered porous media
